doc.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Phone interruption and seasons changing
summary: Phone calls interrupt; Hendricks talks about climate and cosmic perspective.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Tape changes, reel headers and session breaks

blocks.x: Amazing man. I really thought about him until I hit upon just how amazing he was, and it stopped me. I want to tell you about that.
I can’t believe how fast this time has passed.
Oh it did that last time. We seem to talk about 15 minutes and it was gone. When it’s interesting it goes. When it’s not interesting it stands still.

The whole seasonal pattern that we lived with all of our lives and all of our parents’ lives, is going to change. Places that were hot are going to be cold, places that were cold are going to be hot, and I think that’s what this stuff means — snow in the south, snow in Jerusalem. So I think the whole earth is shaking off this last thousand years. I think that’s what it does every thousand years, just like a dog when he jumps in the water, when he comes out he goes — that’s what the earth is doing, and it’s going to shake off all these politicians. I believe it in my soul you know, because I think that’s what it means. I think © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -15-
a person is wise if he watches things cosmically instead of locally. Try to go up into the sun and look down at the earth. Then you can see it a lot better. You see it a lot.
